text:
alex: Heads-up — saw a model import where the chat preamble vanished after hf->redwood convert. Repo: https://huggingface.co/org/newchat (v1). safetensors shards are present; converter completed with exit 0 but the system prompt insertion is empty in runtime. Anyone seen metadata drift like this?

marta: Reproduced locally. converter logs show a schema rename: metadata_version: 2 -> schema:v3 and the key 'preamble' got renamed upstream to 'chat_system' but our keymap didn't include it. config.json ends up missing the chat preamble field.

alex: So converter handles weight key renames but not config key remaps? ping @sam for revpin/hub fetch behavior.

sam: Possible compounding factor: revpin logic allowed fetching the latest snapshot, but org did a force-push and the snapshot manifest at CDN vs git-ref didn't match. I saw the downloader choose manifest A while blobs came from snapshot B. Will dump checksums.

ingest-bot: deploy:importer-run started for org/newchat v1 rev=refs/heads/main

marta: Quick repro command I used: `git-lfs smudge` + `python hf_converter.py --input hf://org/newchat --out redwood:/tmp/newchat` then `jq '.model.chat.preamble' converted/config.json` -> null. Also converter emitted: `WARN missing config key: preamble -> skip`.

alex: Logs also show `WARNING: missing special_tokens['preamble'] - falling back to system_token` which is our fallback but it means the runtime prompt pipeline doesn't insert the intended preamble text. That explains the silent regression in evals.

sam: There's another wrinkle: one of the safetensors shards returned a 200 with empty body due to CDN auth/edge race when downloader used conditional GET + auth header. The partial shard made the merged meta.json miss some keys (the ones we rely on to map chat template).

marta: I captured the curl from edge: ```
> curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://cdn.hf.co/blobs/sha256:abc123"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Length: 0
ETag: "def456"
```
But retrieving the blob body right after yields empty bytes. If a shard's meta section is empty, converter treats it as not having chat metadata.

jung: This rings a bell — hub-downloader reused auth tokens across parallel requests and caches conditional headers. If the token rotated mid-stream the edge returned an empty payload 200. I have a fix to disable `If-None-Match` on auth-protected blob downloads and to avoid reusing stale auth header for parallel fetches.

sam: Short-term workaround: run importer with `--force-revpin` (use commit SHA) and `--parallel-downloads=1` to avoid TTL races; that should avoid the partial shard case. I'll prepare a temp converter image with the revpin flag enforced.

marta: Note: quantization stage is fragile here too. If shard fetch yields truncated tensor shapes, quantizer emits shape mismatch exceptions but converter swallowed them and kept going — so we ended up with a model that loaded but with a renamed/shifted weight layout and missing config keys. I'll add a strict sanity check in quant step to fail hard on any missing tensor keys.

alex: Timeline? Can we patch quick: mapping table for config key rename + revpin enforcement + downloader fix? If PRs are small we can hotfix converter image and reimport.

ingest-bot: deploy:importer-image v2026.03.20-24 pushed to staging

sam: I'll open PR: add mapping 'preamble' -> 'chat_system' to hf-converter keymap, enforce revpin by default for imports that include chat templates, and disable conditional fetch on auth-protected blob endpoints. CI will run full import + eval.

marta: After PR lands I'll re-run import and then run quick evals: sanity for chat preamble presence, 1k prompt samples, and a FP16 quantized run smoke test. If those pass I'll sign off for prod import.

alex: Thanks. Please add a short blurb to release notes and ping support so they know affected users might see no preamble until reimport. Also add an internal note about shard partial-download detection.

sam: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/hf-converter/pulls/412 (contains tests + changelog). Marked for hotfix.

marta: Verified staging import passes with corrected image. Chat preamble present and eval NLL is back to baseline. Will coordinate prod run tomorrow morning.

alex: Great job. Closing loop here — long-term we should add a converter integration test that simulates auth token rotation and a CDN edge returning a 200-empty-body to catch this earlier.

sam: Agreed. I'll add that to the importer test harness. :thumbsup:
